;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights|SOHR]] reports that Syrian government shelling and Russian air strikes occur in several areas in [[Idlib province]], in the first such raids since a September truce deal, killing at least 15 civilians including eight children and wounding around 60. [https://www.trtworld.com/middle-east/regime-shelling-and-russian-air-raids-kill-15-civilians-in-syria-24939?utm_source=GoogleNews&utm_medium=rss (TRT World)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/03/civilians-killed-government-air-strikes-hit-syria-idlib-190314145321261.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019 Lagos school collapse]]
**A building in [[Lagos]], [[Nigeria]], collapses, killing ten people and leaving more than 100 others trapped under the rubble. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-47555373 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-school/100-children-many-others-feared-trapped-in-collapse-of-nigeria-building-that-housed-school-idUSKBN1QU1G7 (Reuters)]
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]] 
**[[Canada]] and the [[United States]] ground all [[Boeing 737 MAX|Boeing 737 Max 8]] and Max 9 aircraft and ban the jet from their airspace until further notice. It is now effectively grounded worldwide, with no operators remaining unaffected by grounding orders. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/garneau-boeing-ethiopia-crash-1.5054234 (CBC)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-47562727 (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/world/live-news/boeing-737-max-8-ethiopia-airlines-crash/index.html (CNN)]
*An avalanche on [[Ben Nevis]] kills two [[France|French]] nationals and a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] national. A fourth climber is injured and is receiving treatment at a hospital in [[Glasgow]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-47553208 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*At least 111 schools in [[Malaysia]] are shut down following the treatment of 200 children, staff, and others being poisoned. Authorities suspect that a chemical dump in the southern state of [[Johor]] is responsible for the sudden illnesses. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-malaysia-poisoning/malaysia-shuts-111-schools-as-poisonings-become-more-critical-idUSKBN1QU0YV (Reuters)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/14/malaysia-shuts-111-schools-as-poisonings-become-more-critical.html (CNBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Killing of Susanna Feldmann]]
**Ali Bashar confesses in court in [[Germany]] to killing teenager Susanna Feldmann. Bashar is a failed asylum seeker from [[Iraq]]. The case prompted national debate and a pledge by [[Angela Merkel]] to call for improvements to the deportation system in Germany. Counterterror police traveled to [[Iraq]] in order to return him to Germany, as he had already been deported when he was identified in connection to the murder; Iraq has [[Iraq-Germany relations|no extradition treaty]] with Germany. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-47536431 (BBC News)] 
*[[Marielle Franco#Final days and assassination|Assassination of Marielle Franco]]
**Two former military police officers are arrested in [[Brazil]] for the murders of [[Marielle Franco]] and her driver Anderson Gomes. One of the suspects was arrested at home, in a Rio de Janeiro [[gated community]] where [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] also resides. Franco was born in a [[Rio de Janeiro|Rio]] [[favela]] and became a politician and activist against violence in the slums, which are often controlled by paramilitary groups. Her assassination prompted widespread protests. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/12/police-officers-arrested-murder-brazilian-politician-marielle-franco (''The Guardian)'']
*[[Suzano school shooting]]
**Two men, aged 17 and 25 years, attack a school in the [[Brazil|Brazilian]] city of [[Suzano]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]], with a revolver and a knife, killing eight and wounding 23 people, among students and staff. The two [[school shooting|shooters]] committed [[suicide]] [[murder-suicide|after]] the attack. Police have found a crossbow, Molotov cocktails and a "suitcase with wires" at the scene. [https://g1.globo.com/sp/mogi-das-cruzes-suzano/noticia/2019/03/13/tiros-deixam-feridos-em-escola-de-suzano.ghtml (G1)]
*[[Trials of Paul Manafort]]
**Former [[Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign|Trump campaign]] manager [[Paul Manafort]] is sentenced to 3½ years for money-laundering and obstruction of justice. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/13/us/politics/paul-manafort-sentencing.html (''The New York Times'')]
**Minutes after Manafort is sentenced in federal court, [[Law of New York (state)|New York state prosecutors]] announce 16 criminal charges against him related to mortgage fraud, conspiracy and falsifying business records. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/13/paul-manafort-indicted-by-ny-prosecutors-after-federal-sentencing.html (CNBC)]
*Iranian human rights activist and lawyer [[Nasrin Sotoudeh]], who won the [[Sakharov Prize]] in 2012, is sentenced to 38 years in prison for her defence of women who had been arrested after [[Girls of Enghelab Street|removing their hijabs]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/13/world/middleeast/nasrin-sotoudeh-iran-lawyer-lashes.amp.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Frank Cali]], the reputed head of the [[Gambino crime family]], is shot dead by an unknown assailant outside his home in [[Todt Hill]], [[Staten Island]], [[New York City]]. It is the first targeted killing of a mob boss in New York City since [[Paul Castellano]] was assassinated in 1985. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-47566382 (BBC News)]
*[[Mexico|Mexican]] authorities announce a national search operation is underway after revealing masked gunmen with a list of names stormed a bus on March 7 as it was traveling along a highway that connects the town of [[San Fernando, Tamaulipas|San Fernando]] with the city of [[Reynosa]]. The perpetrators kidnapped 19 people and they have not been seen since. [https://ktla.com/2019/03/16/investigators-scrambling-to-solve-mystery-just-miles-from-u-s-mexico-border-after-gunmen-take-19-people/ (KTLA)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**The [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|UK's parliament]] votes against a no-deal [[Brexit]]. This greatly increases the chance of a delayed Brexit, to be voted on Thursday, as well as opening the door to the possibility of a second referendum. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/brexit-no-deal-vote-1.5054219 (''CBC'')]

;Science and technology
*A team of physicists at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]], assisted by colleagues in [[Switzerland]] and the [[United States]], successfully returns the state of a [[quantum computer]] a fraction of a second into the past. [https://phys.org/news/2019-03-physicists-reverse-quantum.html (Phys.org)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/time-reverse-quantum-computer-science-study-moscow-a8820516.html (''The Independent'')]

;Sports
*[[Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race]]
**[[Peter Kaiser (musher)|Peter Kaiser]] wins the 2019, 1000-mile Iditarod, arriving in [[Nome, Alaska|Nome]] in 9 days, 12 hours and 39 minutes. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-alaska-iditarod/alaskan-musher-wins-his-first-iditarod-crossing-finish-line-in-nome-idUSKBN1QU1OC (Reuters)]
